questions.title: Composition of Nissl bodies
questions.question: Nissl bodies consist of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Synaptic vesicles are small membrane-bound sacs of neurotransmitter clustered at the axon terminal (presynaptic bouton), not the basophilic cytoplasmic masses of the perikaryon that are stained as Nissl bodies.
explanations.B: Correct. Nissl bodies (Nissl substance) are the basophilic granular masses of the neuronal cell body and dendrites, composed of rough endoplasmic reticulum studded with ribosomes together with free polyribosomes. Their abundant ribosomal RNA is what gives them their strong basophilia and reflects the neuron's high rate of protein synthesis. They extend into the dendrites but are absent from the axon hillock and axon, a classic identifying feature, and their dispersal (chromatolysis) after axonal injury mirrors this protein-synthesising role.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The Golgi apparatus is a separate organelle that packages and modifies proteins; it is argyrophilic (silver-staining) rather than basophilic and is not what the term Nissl body denotes.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Lysosomes and lipofuscin (an age-related residual-body pigment) are distinct cytoplasmic components; lipofuscin does accumulate with age in neurons but is not the basophilic Nissl substance.

questions.learning_objective: State that Nissl bodies are composed of rough endoplasmic reticulum and ribosomes (including free polyribosomes), accounting for their cytoplasmic basophilia.

questions.title: Location of bipolar neurons
questions.question: Bipolar neurons are present in:

options.D: Mesencephalic nucleus of the trigeminal nerve

explanations.A: Correct. Bipolar neurons carry two processes — a single dendrite and a single axon — extending from opposite poles of the cell body, and in the adult they occur in the special sensory pathways: the retina, the olfactory epithelium, and the vestibular (Scarpa's) and cochlear (spiral) ganglia of the vestibulocochlear nerve. The vestibular ganglion is therefore the correct location among the options offered. This bipolar morphology suits their role as a first-order relay in a sensory pathway.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The neurons of the spinal (dorsal root) ganglia are pseudounipolar — a single process leaves the cell body and divides into central and peripheral branches — not bipolar.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Sympathetic (autonomic) ganglion cells are multipolar neurons with many dendrites, not bipolar.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The mesencephalic nucleus of the trigeminal nerve contains pseudounipolar primary sensory neurons (a unique CNS location for such cells), not bipolar neurons.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the vestibular (and cochlear) ganglia as sites of bipolar neurons, distinguishing them from the pseudounipolar spinal ganglia and mesencephalic nucleus and the multipolar sympathetic ganglia.

questions.title: Unencapsulated sensory nerve ending
questions.question: One of the following is classified as unencapsulated:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The Golgi tendon organ is an encapsulated proprioceptor enclosed in a connective-tissue capsule at the myotendinous junction.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Meissner's (tactile) corpuscles are encapsulated mechanoreceptors of the dermal papillae, wrapped in a thin connective-tissue capsule.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Krause end bulbs are encapsulated receptors, a coiled nerve terminal surrounded by a thin connective-tissue capsule.
explanations.D: Correct. Sensory nerve endings are classified as encapsulated (enclosed in a connective-tissue capsule — Meissner, Pacinian, Ruffini and Krause corpuscles and the Golgi tendon organ) or unencapsulated (naked terminals lacking such a capsule). Free nerve endings are the prototypical unencapsulated ending: bare terminal branches, mostly of pain and temperature fibres, ramifying among epithelial and connective-tissue cells without any capsule. Merkel discs and peritrichial (hair-follicle) endings are the other unencapsulated types.

questions.learning_objective: Classify free nerve endings as unencapsulated sensory receptors, distinguishing them from the encapsulated Golgi tendon organ, Meissner's corpuscle and Krause end bulb.
